opex.text: In addition to higher credit losses, UACC’s ability to achieve profitability has been negatively affected by increased operating expenses and productivity challenges. Also, we have identified vulnerabilities in certain IT systems and determined additional investment will be needed to update and secure those systems. We are undertaking a number of initiatives designed to reduce operating expenses, introduce improved processes, and reporting metrics across UACC’s operations, invest in IT systems, improve origination and servicing productivity, and leverage CarStory data to improve underwriting and servicing performance. We intend to grow UACC’s business profitably by reducing credit losses, increasing UACC’s market share, and streamlining its operations.

sm.text: Build a world class sales and marketing program by attracting and retaining the best dealers and driving deeper dealer engagement to enable growth. In 2025, our technology teams made substantial progress towards modernizing our infrastructure to drive speed and scalability. This included a complete overhaul of Fast Lane, UACC’s online dealer portal. Launched in early 2026, this upgraded platform leverages direct dealer feedback to minimize friction, increase application volume, and streamline the user experience.

da_op.heading: Depreciation and amortization
da_op.text: Depreciation and amortization increased $0.6 million to $1.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $0.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily as a result of an increase in property and equipment, net to $7.8 million as of September 30, 2026 from $5.5 million as of September 30, 2025.

prov.heading: Ability to manage credit losses
prov.text: While credit losses are inherent in the automotive finance receivables business, several variables have negatively affected UACC’s recent loss and delinquency rates, including higher interest rates since COVID, the current inflationary environment and vehicle depreciation, which has negatively impacted the fair value of our finance receivables and the losses recognized. While we are beginning to see some improvements in our more recently issued finance receivable vintages and we expect long term improvements in our overall finance receivable portfolio, we expect some downward trends to continue to negatively impact our business for the remainder of 2026. UACC primarily operates in the non-prime sector of the market which tends to have more volatility. In 2020 and 2021, COVID related stimulus and used vehicle appreciation resulted in significantly lower delinquencies and subsequent losses. In late 2022 and 2023, delinquencies and loss rates rose as a result of the aforementioned factors and, in response, we implemented changes to tighten our credit program. We initially saw some improvements with the 2023 and 2024 vintages as a result of these changes. Subsequently, macroeconomic factors negatively impacted these vintages.

nonint.text: In addition to higher credit losses, UACC’s ability to achieve profitability has been negatively affected by increased operating expenses and productivity challenges. Also, we have identified vulnerabilities in certain IT systems and determined additional investment will be needed to update and secure those systems. We are undertaking a number of initiatives designed to reduce operating expenses, introduce improved processes, and reporting metrics across UACC’s operations, invest in IT systems, improve origination and servicing productivity, and leverage CarStory data to improve underwriting and servicing performance. We intend to grow UACC’s business profitably by reducing credit losses, increasing UACC’s market share, and streamlining its operations.

nonop.heading: Interest expense
nonop.text:
Interest expense primarily includes interest expense on UACC's Warehouse Credit Facilities, interest expense incurred on securitization debt, and interest expense on financing of beneficial interests in securitizations.

Interest expense decreased $1.4 million, or 10.4%, to $11.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $13.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily as a result of lower interest expense incurred on the securitization debt attributable to a lower outstanding principal balance of $414.3 million as of September 30, 2026, as compared to $465.8 million as of September 30, 2025.

net.heading: Adjusted net income (loss)
net.text:
We calculate Adjusted net income (loss) as net income (loss) from continuing operations less preferred stock dividends attributable to noncontrolling interests of subsidiary, adjusted for stock compensation expense, severance expense, bankruptcy costs (which represent professional fees incurred related to the bankruptcy prior to filing of the petition and post-emergence), reorganization items, net (which relate to certain charges incurred during the bankruptcy proceedings, such as legal and professional fees incurred directly as a result of the bankruptcy proceeding, the write-off of deferred financing costs and discount on debt subject to compromise and other related charges), operating lease right-of-use assets impairment and long-lived asset impairment charges.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: Net cash flows provided by operating activities from continuing operations increased by $7.5 million, from $50.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to $58.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. The increase was primarily due to a $14.3 million decrease in originations of finance receivables held for sale. As a result of emerging from the Prepackaged Chapter 11 Case and applying fresh start accounting, our finance receivables are originated and accounted for as held for investment at fair value and are classified as investing activities prospectively. The increase in net cash flows provided by operating activities was partially offset by a decrease in principal payments received on finance receivables held for sale of $6.5 million.

da.heading: Depreciation and amortization
da.text: Depreciation and amortization increased $0.6 million to $1.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $0.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily as a result of an increase in property and equipment, net to $7.8 million as of September 30, 2026 from $5.5 million as of September 30, 2025.

capex.text: Depreciation and amortization increased $0.6 million to $1.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $0.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily as a result of an increase in property and equipment, net to $7.8 million as of September 30, 2026 from $5.5 million as of September 30, 2025.

net sales.heading: CarStory revenue
net sales.text:
CarStory generates advertiser, publisher and other user service revenue by offering its AI-powered analytics and digital retailing services to dealers, automotive financial services companies and others in the automotive industry.

CarStory revenue remained flat at $1.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025.

Net interest income.text: Adjusted net loss decreased $19.5 million to $16.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from $35.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to higher net interest income after losses and recoveries, partially offset by lower noninterest income and higher expenses, as discussed above.

Noninterest income.text: Adjusted net loss decreased $19.5 million to $16.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from $35.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to higher net interest income after losses and recoveries, partially offset by lower noninterest income and higher expenses, as discussed above.

intro.text: Vroom, Inc. is a holding company that conducts its operations through its subsidiaries. Unless the context otherwise requires, references herein to “Vroom”, the "Company”, “we”, “us” or “our” refer to Vroom and its consolidated subsidiaries. The Company was incorporated in Delaware on January 31, 2012, under the name BCM Partners III, Corp. On June 25, 2013, the Company changed its name to Auto America, Inc., and on July 9, 2015, the Company changed its name to Vroom, Inc. The Company previously operated an end-to-end ecommerce platform to buy and sell used vehicles through its subsidiary Vroom Automotive, LLC.

lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.
